<pasted_content id="6554">
I checked it, and the update prompt does not pop up on its own.
What I did:

1. I quit the installed JusPrin 2.0.0 on your Mac and set `jusprin_update_last_attempt` to `"0"` in its settings file. I saved a copy of the file first at `/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/710d8e8d-0d6b-4a8f-9d8f-a3910b8238b8/scratchpad/JusPrin2.conf.before-update-test`. On the Mac this file has no checksum line, so the edit was safe.
2. I started 2.0.0 again. 12 seconds after starting, its log said “JusPrin’s update check: found 2.0.1”.
3. I waited until the app had been running for over a minute, then looked at every window it had.

What I saw:

* The app showed only its usual windows. No update dialog or prompt opened.
* Home looks exactly as it did before the check. The gear icon at the top right has no dot or badge either.
* The update shows up only if someone opens Preferences and looks: a dot beside “Updates”, and on that page the “JusPrin 2.0.1 is available” card. This matches the code, where the Preferences window is the only part of the app that receives the update check’s result.

So someone on 2.0.0 who never opens Preferences won’t learn that 2.0.1 exists. The app ran the new check itself and saved its normal settings, so there’s nothing to restore. 2.0.0 is still running.
</pasted_content id="6554">

OrcaSlicer's update check is replaced by JusPrin's: app_update_check
hands it over, so OrcaSlicer's request never goes out and its "new
version" window no longer opens at startup. JusPrin asks its own GitHub
releases once a day (Updates/UpdateCheck, ReleaseFeed, UpdateRecord) and
compares against its own version, 2.0.0 (Updates/Version.hpp).

Preferences > Updates shows the result: up to date, checking, couldn't
check, or a new version with its release notes, "Download" (opens the
release page; nothing is installed in the app yet) and "Skip this
version". The "New JusPrin versions" checkbox switches the daily check
off and carries the privacy note. A Microsoft Store install says its
updates come from the Store. Help > Check for Updates runs the check and
opens Updates.

Rules that follow:

- **No pill is the all-clear, and it is never given before a check.** The pill is drawn only while OrcaSlicer reports an issue, ignored ones included. While OrcaSlicer holds an unapplied edit the last issues are kept, the pill says it is checking and both buttons are off, so the pill does not go until OrcaSlicer has looked. An issue that was not in the list before is announced once by a ring that spreads from the pill twice; an edit that keeps an issue, and ignoring one or undoing that, announce nothing.
- **Nothing is resolved by the fork.** An issue goes when OrcaSlicer lets go of its notification. An agent saying it fixed something changes nothing.
- **"Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's answer.** An error-level notification blocks. For the slice result it is OrcaSlicer's own post-slice check, which allows a path 2 mm past the plate edge; the monitor does not apply a stricter test of its own.
- **The object is never read out of the words.** Two messages of one kind are told apart by comparing OrcaSlicer's words now with its words before, as OrcaSlicer does itself. Which object a message is about always comes from a check's own ids.
- **A press acts on what is true at the press**, and with no assistant set up it sends nothing and offers the chat panel's setup. **One button, one question**: Ask AI sends "Explain this issue and my options." with the issue as context, and the turn gets the ordinary tools, so the person asks for a fix in the chat. A second "Resolve with AI" button was removed on 2026-10-28: it sent the same context with the same tools and differed only in the sentence, which the person could not tell apart.
- **Slice-result warnings follow OrcaSlicer's send dialog.** The warnings the G-code processor stores on a slice result (bed temperature, nozzle hardness, timelapse) are shown as OrcaSlicer's Bambu send dialog shows them, the only place OrcaSlicer itself shows them: never the bed-temperature one, the traditional-timelapse one once although it is stored twice. The chip and `slice_report` read one fork-owned table, `Workspace/SliceResultWarnings`, whose comment says why it is a copy and not an upstream seam, and a guard test fails when OrcaSlicer defines a kind the table does not classify. The timelapse ones apply only to a print that records a timelapse, which is chosen when it is sent: `slice_report` and Check print list them marked so, and the chip does not count them.
- **Operation failures are not print issues.** A failed download or a refused arrange is a confirmation, never an entry in the issue list.
- **Closing hides, it never resolves.** The pill is always there and is the way back; the list and the bubble are opened and closed, one at a time, and closing either changes nothing about the issue or the count. The list closes on a pick, a second press of the pill, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to the selection: opening it selects its object, and it closes when that object stops being selected, which is what a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do in OrcaSlicer. Turning the view or dragging the object leaves it open. Its close button leaves the selection alone, and a press on **Ask AI** that reaches the chat closes it. With one issue the pill opens the bubble directly, and with several the bubble's pager walks them all. The overlay hears Escape and presses through handlers of its own on the canvas's window, bound after OrcaSlicer's and so called first; no OrcaSlicer file is involved.
- **Ignoring a warning is the person's mark, not OrcaSlicer's.** **Ignore this warning** in the bubble leaves OrcaSlicer's notification alone: the warning stays in the list, marked, below the ones that count, and the pill stops counting it ("1 warning ignored" when nothing else is left, never "No print issues"). Only a warning can be ignored; a blocker cannot, because OrcaSlicer would still refuse to print. An ignore lasts while OrcaSlicer keeps reporting that warning on the active plate's own list, and is forgotten when OrcaSlicer stops, so a warning that comes back is shown again. It is not saved with the project. The rule is `mark_ignored` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue`.

Known limits: application and account notifications (update available, plug-in missing, preset sync conflict) are routed to `App` and drawn nowhere yet. A confirmation shows OrcaSlicer's words and a close button; the actions OrcaSlicer attached to its own notification (open folder, eject, cancel an upload) are not offered. Only a slice has a percentage and a known ending; other work shows a bar with no amount and is recorded as done unless its Cancel was pressed. Uploads and downloads have not been run. The tips and the object size card are not shown.

### Agent WebView

The production Agent interface is a separate React/TypeScript package that runs locally inside a `wxWebView`. It needs:

- a versioned schema for commands and events;
- scripted mock conversations that play back the same way every time, for UI tests;
127:Print again sends a recorded G-code's kept file, never a fresh slice, and always through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog, where the person presses Send. A Bambu printer takes a `.gcode.3mf`, so a Bambu print also keeps the package it uploaded (`<hash>.gcode.3mf`, and for a cloud printer the config 3MF it also sent), byte for byte, with its SHA-256 on the send (`packageHash`); it goes when its G-code's copy is pruned. Print again parses that package, hands it to Select Machine through `Plater::update_print_required_data` and `EVT_PRINT_FROM_SDCARD_VIEW` (the printer file browser's print-from-storage mode, which draws the plate, picture and filaments from the file), and sets the dialog's new-print flag (`SelectMachineDialog::set_required_data_new_print`, the one upstream seam), so the job uploads the local file as a new print instead of asking the printer to print by name. Printing from the printer's storage is not used: the file name on the printer is reused per project, so it cannot say which version would print. A print host with OrcaSlicer's standard upload dialog is sent a temporary copy of the kept G-code (the queue deletes what it uploads); ElegooLink, Creality Print, Flashforge's local API and `use_3mf` hosts are not offered Print again. `GcodeHistoryRecorder::print_again_state` decides whether it is offered for the printer selected now; a kept file whose hash no longer matches is never sent and the entry says so. `print_dialog_open` opens the same dialogs for the agent: a plate's slice, or with `gcode` a recorded G-code.

input.recap: The missing update prompt is intended, not a bug. JusPrin's update check finds 2.0.1, but the design decided on 2026-10-22 shows the result only in Preferences › Updates, and the code matches. I changed nothing. Whether to show it anywhere else is your call.
input.ask: Should JusPrin tell people about a new version outside Preferences?

content.text:
The update check works. JusPrin 2.0.0 never pops up a prompt because it was designed that way: the result only ever appears in Preferences › Updates. I changed nothing.

**What the code does.** In [UpdateCheck.cpp](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp), the app checks GitHub 10 seconds after it starts, then again every hour. A check only runs if the last successful one was more than a day ago. When the check finds a newer version it saves it to the settings file and tells whoever is listening. Only one part of the app listens: the Preferences window ([PreferencesWindow.cpp:186](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp:186)). That window draws the dot beside "Updates" and the "JusPrin 2.0.1 is available" card. Home, the project screen, the gear icon and the chat never hear about it. Before JusPrin, OrcaSlicer had its own "new version" window that opened at startup. JusPrin turned that check off on purpose so OrcaSlicer's server is never asked ([ShellController.cpp:2094](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:2094)). So nothing else shows an update either.

**Where the design came from.** The JusPrin v2 design canvas has a note dated 2026-10-22 next to the Updates boards. It says the result shows "only here, plus the dot on Updates". It also says "Nothing pops up, and nothing appears in a project or in chat." The commit that added the check, 80ed1692ff on 2026-10-23, follows that note. I couldn't find your own words behind it: the session where it was decided isn't in the searchable transcripts. So it's unverified whether you chose "no pop-up" yourself or it was a proposal that got written down as decided.

**What this means for people already on 2.0.0.** Anything we change now only ships in a later release. People running 2.0.0 or 2.0.1 keep today's behaviour until they update by hand. Inside the app there's one other way to reach them. The server can refuse an old version, and the app then shows a "Get the new version…" button on the chat, sign-in and model picker. But that blocks their account, so it only makes sense when an old version really has to stop working. For the people on 2.0.0 now, the realistic routes are outside the app: an email, or a post where they already follow JusPrin.

**Decision needed: should JusPrin tell people about a new version anywhere besides Preferences?** It's your call because it changes what people see on screens outside Preferences, and the current design says nothing pops up.
- **Keep it as is.** Costs nothing. Most people will never find out a new version exists.
- **Put a dot on the gear icon on Home and on the project screen.** Small and quiet, about a day of work. It's still easy to miss, because the dot doesn't say what it means.
- **Show a one-line notice on Home once per new version.** For example: "JusPrin 2.0.1 is available", with Download and Skip buttons. It never appears inside a project or during a print. About a day or two of work plus new design boards. People can't miss it, and they can dismiss it.

My pick is the once-per-version notice on Home. If you agree, I'll draw the boards on the canvas first and build after you've seen them.
